annotation.evidence_span: except when a server has requested closure of the request stream with this error code
annotation.interpretation_a: The client can only send HTTP_REQUEST_REJECTED if the server *actively* signaled closure using that error code on the stream. Any other rejection must be HTTP_REQUEST_CANCELLED.
annotation.interpretation_b: The client can send HTTP_REQUEST_REJECTED in any situation where the server has *at any point* requested closure of the request stream, even if the server didn't use HTTP_REQUEST_REJECTED to do so. The server could have used a different error code to request closure, and the client is still permitted to respond with HTTP_REQUEST_REJECTED.
annotation.justification: The phrase 'requested closure of the request stream with this error code' is ambiguous. 'This error code' could refer to the server requesting closure *using* HTTP_REQUEST_REJECTED, or simply requesting closure in any way.
annotation.missing_information: It is unclear whether the server's request for closure must be signaled *with* the HTTP_REQUEST_REJECTED error code, or merely *any* request for closure.
